Add group-return rosters: the subordinate names the BMF throws away

Source: R/md-ingest-affiliate-listing.R
md_ingest_affiliate_listing.Rd

When a central organisation files a group return it attaches a roster naming every subordinate covered - AffiliateListing/AffiliateListingGrp in the XML, with name, EIN and address for each. It is the only source that states a group's membership as a list rather than leaving it to be inferred from a shared GEN.

Usage

md_ingest_affiliate_listing(
  con = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  guard = TRUE,
  version = "v2009-2013"
)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

path

Path to a derived affiliate-listing-*.csv. NULL looks in the version source directory, preferring the published tables.

guard

Run md_guard_observed() on the observed rows of source efile990.

version

Pinned efile_affiliate_listing version, e.g. "v3_1".

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

This is the source that recovers subordinate names

GROUP-STRUCTURE-FINDINGS.md §4 measured the problem: the BMF assigns most subordinates the parent's legal name. Of 1,068 TY2013 affiliates matched to the BMF, 803 (75.2%) carry a BMF name different from the one they report for themselves, and in 70% of group returns every member shares one identical BMF name. Five Einstein subordinates all read "ALBERT EINSTEIN HEALTHCARE NETWORK" in the BMF while calling themselves "Belmont Center For Comprehensive Tr", "Einstein Practice Plan Inc" and so on.

So a subordinate's own name is usually absent from the reference entirely, and this roster is where it lives. In a held-out retrieval test (§5) these tokens were 0.19% of the index and carried 23% of the gain - the best return per row measured anywhere in that work.

The names therefore land as observed variants on the subordinates' own EINs. That is the narrow §10 exception, not a breach of it: the roster states the subordinate's own name, not the parent's, so registering it aliases nothing. The parent's name is never copied onto a member.

Two inputs

the published table, or the old extract: From e-file v2_3 on, the roster is a published table, F9-P00-T01-AFFILIATE-LISTING-<year>.CSV, covering every year (30,143 rows for 2009-2025 in v3_1). When sources/efile_affiliate_listing/<version>/ holds those files, they are read. Otherwise the function falls back to the earlier derived extract, affiliate-listing-2009-2013.csv, produced from raw XML before the table existed. Both are pinned like any other source.

The element was renamed in 2013

Returns through TY2012 use AffiliateListing/Affiliate with Name/, AddressUS/ and NameControl; TY2013 onward uses AffiliateListing/AffiliateListingGrp with BusinessName/, USAddress/ and BusinessNameControlTxt. The extract normalises both by matching on the field suffix. A run that returns rows for 2013 only has silently hit the rename.


  2009    260 rows /  21 filings
  2010  1,630 rows /  66 filings
  2011  1,276 rows /  79 filings
  2012  1,204 rows /  88 filings
  2013  1,070 rows /  99 filings
  ----------------------------------
         5,440 rows / 353 filings / 2,515 distinct subordinate EINs

Coverage is thin by construction: only 99 of 483 TY2013 group filers itemise members at all. This source is precise, not comprehensive.

Direction and self-references

The filer of a group return is the central organisation, so the edge is (filer, member, group_member) - the same direction as every other group source. Rows where a filer lists its own EIN are self-loops and are dropped.
